_note: Prepared 2026-10-31 for germomics.com /data. Every number was read from the cited source; see SOURCES.md for what was fetched and how it was checked.

source.label: Deaths (bars) on Snow's 1855 map as digitized by Dodson and Tobler (1992), amended and georeferenced (QGIS thin plate spline to OpenStreetMap, WGS 84) in the R package cholera by lindbrook, data set fatalities.anchor

map.method: One point per address (the 321 'anchor' cases, each the base of a stack of bars on Snow's map); value = deaths at that address (case.count), summing to all 578 bars; label = street of the nearest road segment (latlong.ortho.anchor road.segment joined to roads.name).

source.label: Water pumps on Snow's 1855 map, georeferenced, R package cholera by lindbrook, data set pumps (street names from Snow's map)

pumps.method: All 13 pumps on Snow's map with lindbrook's longitude and latitude; value 0 so they can share the DataPoint shape. Pump 7 is the Broad Street pump.

timelines.title: Fatal cholera attacks per day, Soho, 19 August to 30 September 1854
timelines.alt: Fatal attacks were one a day or fewer until 30 August, jumped to 56 on 31 August and peaked at 143 on 1 September, then fell below 10 a day by 10 September. Another 45 attacks had no known date.

source.label: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd ed. (London: John Churchill, 1855), Table I, p. 49; data via HistData Snow.dates, checked against the Wellcome Library scan

timelines.method: Snow's Table I 'No. of Fatal Attacks' column for 19 Aug to 30 Sep 1854, as printed; the 45 attacks with 'Date unknown' are left out of the line (571 dated + 45 undated = 616).

timelines.title: Cholera deaths per day, Soho, 19 August to 30 September 1854
timelines.alt: Deaths peaked at 127 on 2 September, the day after attacks peaked, and fell to 18 by 10 September and 6 on 12 September; all 616 deaths are dated.

source.label: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd ed. (London: John Churchill, 1855), Table I, p. 49; data via HistData Snow.dates, checked against the Wellcome Library scan

timelines.method: Snow's Table I 'Deaths' column for 19 Aug to 30 Sep 1854, as printed; it sums to 616 with no undated deaths.

source.label: Deaths (bars) on Snow's 1855 map as digitized by Dodson and Tobler (1992), amended and georeferenced (QGIS thin plate spline to OpenStreetMap, WGS 84) in the R package cholera by lindbrook, data set fatalities.anchor

table.method: The 321 addresses grouped by the street name lindbrook gives their road segment; the 15 streets with the most deaths, then all other streets together; roman numerals and slashes are lindbrook's names for streets that share a name or changed name.

timelines.title: Influenza deaths per week, London, June 1918 to May 1919
timelines.alt: Three waves of civilian influenza deaths in London: a summer peak of 279 in the week ending 13 July 1918, an autumn peak of 2,651 in the week ending 2 November 1918, and a late-winter peak of 825 in the week ending 1 March 1919.

source.label: Registrar-General, Report on the Mortality from Influenza in England and Wales during the Epidemic of 1918-19, Supplement to the 81st Annual Report (London: HMSO, 1920, Cmd. 700), Table XX, pp. 48-50, London (Administrative County)

timelines.method: Deaths of civilians in the Administrative County of London certified to influenza, for each of the 46 weeks ending 29 Jun 1918 to 10 May 1919, as printed; they sum to the table's wave totals (997, 12,330, 3,786) and whole-period total (17,113).

timelines.title: Influenza death rate, London, June 1918 to May 1919
timelines.alt: London's weekly influenza death rate, expressed as an annual rate, reached 3.7 per 1,000 in July 1918, 35.0 per 1,000 in the week ending 2 November 1918 and 10.9 per 1,000 in the week ending 1 March 1919.

source.label: Registrar-General, Report on the Mortality from Influenza in England and Wales during the Epidemic of 1918-19, Supplement to the 81st Annual Report (London: HMSO, 1920, Cmd. 700), Table XX, pp. 48-50, London (Administrative County)

timelines.method: Same table, the italic row: each week's civilian influenza deaths as an annual death rate per 1,000 civilians living in the Administrative County of London, as printed.

source.label: Registrar-General, Report on the Mortality from Influenza in England and Wales during the Epidemic of 1918-19, Supplement to the 81st Annual Report (London: HMSO, 1920, Cmd. 700), Table XX, pp. 48-50, London (Administrative County)

table.method: The table's own wave and whole-period columns for London (Administrative County), civilians, as printed; the weekly rows sum to these totals.

influenza-1918.cases_note: The Registrar-General's report tabulates deaths only and gives no weekly count of influenza cases for London; I found no case series for the same place and measure, so none is included.
